newsitem.title: UK: LME copper rechallenges upside on wary pre-market.
newsitem.headline: LME copper rechallenges upside on wary pre-market.

text.p: LME copper clawed higher in jittery pre-market activity on Friday, underpinned by solid nearby spreads that were expected to flare as more shorts seek to cover their positions, traders said.
The cash/threes spread was indicated at a $210/$220 backwardation, up from $198/$203 at the end of trade on Thursday.
Most of the tightness was from late April to early May with the cash/May spread ending at a $99/$105 backwardation on Thursday.
"Everyone's a bit anxious about the spreads," a trader said.
"I think there'll be some more covering today since people don't usually want it to come to cash, when the longs will make the shorts come to them," he added.
For the cash/one-day spread, the LME has imposed a limit of one percent of the previous day's cash settlement.
The first crunch date was expected to be traded on Monday, traders said.
Three months ticked higher in thin dealings to $2,382, up $14 from Thursday's afternoon kerb close, after a 1,550-tonne stocks fall.
It was expected to have another go at $2,400 after failing to break through the level on Thursday.
Aluminium rechallenged $1,600 after inventories dropped by 2,600 tonnes, and was last indicated at $1,601/4 after $1,594 on Thursday.
The market probably needed to consolidate before it would be able to gather enough strength to convincingly break above that psychological level, analysts said.
Other markets were little changed in early dealings.
Zinc shrugged off a 2,775-tonne stocks rise, edging to $1,274, up $3. The stocks build was not surprising since Chinese deliveries of the metal had been expected to enter warehouses, one dealer said.
Tin was indicated slightly higher at $5,735/65 from $5,720 while lead was steady at $635/38 compared to $636.
Nickel was unchanged at $7,450/60 after $7,450 and alloy was little changed at $1,485/95.
